accuracy.reason: All eight objectives hold: reuse and costs, hit/miss actors, input-sensitive keys, old-fill race, TTL/eviction, local/shared copies, stampede/outage limits and workload fit. Primary sources support boundaries; authoritative database assumptions are explicitly in prerequisites.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

mechanisms.reason: The cache-aside flow, independent database/delete steps, delayed old fill and source-work amplification are traceable. Both diagrams match the text; the stale-copy diagram illustrates state before removal and does not claim deletion guarantees freshness.

evidence.quote: A reader can fetch $20 before the update, pause, then refill $20 after removal.

coherence.reason: Declared database, concurrent instances, latency/capacity and post-commit-read prerequisites are sufficient. Copy ownership precedes read/key behavior, then stale fills and disappearance precede topology/failure choice. Every card objective is taught.

evidence.quote: The API checks and fills the cache explicitly. The cache does not fetch the result from the database on its own.

decisions.reason: Provides measured fit, currency/private-result key scope, authoritative acceptance for fresh prices, local/shared costs and safe bounded fallback with rejection. Learner makes workload-specific choices and does not invent cache availability during outage.

evidence.quote: Limit fallback work to what the database can handle; reject excess requests or serve older data only where the application permits stale results.

clarity.reason: Hit, miss, cache-aside, key, invalidation, TTL, eviction, locality, stampede and hit ratio are explained before use. Price race and eviction distinction give useful concrete transfer. Assigned diagrams and shared dialog/CSS inspected only.

evidence.quote: If requests rarely reuse results, or freshness is too hard to maintain, the cache may cost more than it saves.

outcomes.reason: All five criteria supported: repeated expensive guides, station/language key, application-owned hit/miss/fill, and added lookup/write/storage/currentness costs without assuming miss latency improvement.

All four criteria supported: C gets old hours after A refills, deletion cannot cancel A, no read-after-write guarantee, and authoritative bypass under the declared commit prerequisite prevents this cached stale response.
All four criteria supported: 12:03 stale hit, 12:11 expired miss, 12:05 eviction miss, entry lifetime versus source freshness/presence, and later reader-driven fetch rather than automatic refresh.

All five criteria supported: untouched local copies survive, shared-entry deletion fits stated assumptions, network versus in-process access, shared operating/outage cost, and one-local versus all-shared loss of cache access without claiming mandatory application failure.

All five criteria supported: simultaneous duplicate reads, one coalesced pending lookup shared by waiters, 10000 versus 500 overload, aggregate cap/rejection, and stale copy only if independently available and within 60 seconds.

All five criteria supported: reject cache now, no second read to benefit, ample read-cost/capacity headroom, concrete operations/storage costs, and reconsider repeated expensive/capacity-constrained reads with measurement.

sourceChecks.claim: Microsoft caching introduction explicitly favors repeatedly read, relatively stable, expensive/contended data; copy management and resource costs remain. Database authority is an explicit scope assumption rather than a universal cache-store property.
Microsoft cache-aside steps specify application lookup, datastore miss retrieval, fill then return; consistency section rejects unconditional source/cache consistency.

Microsoft caching keyspace examples distinguish entities/types and application-owned fill. Answer-changing inputs must distinguish reusable results; sharing private results across callers violates that identity.

Microsoft cache-aside describes source-write then invalidation and warns consistency is not guaranteed. The lesson independently traces a valid overlapping old read/fill that deletion cannot cancel; authoritative validation follows its declared source semantics.

Redis eviction documents memory-triggered removal, LRU approximation and noeviction error behavior; Microsoft expiration guidance confirms per-key timeout removal. Expiration/eviction do not execute a fetch, and TTL does not bound how old fetched source data was.

AWS caching article explicitly discusses independent in-memory inconsistency, external Redis/Memcached sharing, network/operating dependency and outage consequences; a process restart affects its own in-memory state.
AWS thundering-herd section defines simultaneous uncached requests and coalescing one pending fetch; outage discussion prescribes capping downstream rate/load shedding and testing without cache.

Microsoft caching suitability and AWS cost/latency/reuse guidance support measuring benefits and rejecting low-reuse caches; hit ratio and miss costs are meaningful only with workload and freshness constraints.
